reports.title: RadNet Reports Third Quarter Financial Results with Record Quarterly Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA(1) and Revises Upwards 2026 Financial Guidance Ranges

guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance Update
section: RadNet amends its previously announced guidance levels as follows:

desk.headline: Record revenue up 22% to $638.3m, in line; adjusted EPS $0.30 beat; 2026 imaging outlook raised for a third time
results: Revenue rose 22.1% to a record $638.3m, essentially matching the $639.2m estimate, helped by new centers, acquisitions, joint ventures and better commercial pricing.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 23.8% to $105.0m and the margin edged up to 16.5%; adjusted EPS of $0.30 beat the $0.22 estimate, though GAAP EPS was $0.05 after one-off charges.
MRI, CT and PET/CT volumes rose 19.9% (8.9% at existing centers), lifting advanced imaging to 30.6% of all scans from 28.2%.
Digital Health (AI and imaging software) revenue grew 32.6% to $32.9m, but its adjusted EBITDA dipped to $3.0m from $3.5m.
The balance sheet stays strong with $750.6m of cash and net debt at 1.66 times adjusted EBITDA.

guidance.summary: RadNet raised its 2026 Imaging Center ranges for revenue, adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow for the third quarter running, and nudged up Digital Health EBITDA. Digital Health revenue guidance was kept.

points: Digital Health annual recurring revenue reached about $113m, up 67%, with a sales pipeline above $300m; management expects year-end ARR above $140m.
The pending ONRAD teleradiology deal is projected at $190–200m of revenue and $60–65m of EBITDA in year one and will form a third segment.
Final 2027 Medicare rates cut the fee base by about 2.3%, which management put at roughly a $5m revenue hit.
Ten new centers are now expected to open in 2026, up from seven, while faster scanners and remote technologists add capacity.
Staff shortages for technologists and radiologists keep pressure on wages; full 2027 guidance is due in late February.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 9 Nov 2026

watch: Closing and integration of the ONRAD acquisition.
Whether Digital Health growth starts to lift its margins as recurring revenue builds.
The impact of the 2027 Medicare cut and any action by Congress before year-end.
